questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was very interested in living in a different European culture and I've always wanted to live in Italy, which made me choose Milano.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found most information on my own and everything worked out fine, but I didn't find i

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't really receive a proper introduction, because it was cancelled due to Covid. This of course made my start a bit more confusing, stressful and hectic. Very basic stuff like finding the different campuses, classrooms, toilets etc., was difficult, and I would have been nice with a bit more information on simply getting around and being a student at Unimi. But I reached out to the Erasmus coordinator per mail whenever I had issues or questions and usually got a quick reply. In general I received all necessary information right on time, but it meant a lot of communication per mail.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The housing situation in Milano is not great and there seems to be a lot of scams and very expensive apartments. This made it difficult searching for an apartment from home, but I ended up finding one through the Facebook group: Danskere i Milano.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's a great way to experience different parts of the cities and allows you to integrate more in the Italian everyday life with old neighbor's saying goodmorning - but It might be expensive if you book through a bureau, since they charge a lot of fees.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I dont' really know what housing was offered.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I found my classes online and received an email with instructions on how to enroll a few days before the lectures started. This seemed a bit late to me, but it didn't seem important to enroll early. You write your classes in a sort of document and it was quite easy to do and to change afterwards.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus coordinator could help and my teachers were in general very helpful too.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had a bit of difficulty with choosing classes because I looked at a lot of trimester course (which are early winter/late spring), but I didn't know that from home. In the end it worked out but I had one overlap, where I just skipped lectures every second week.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go to a lot of different lectures the first week before you make your final decision.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took four course and I learned a lot from the two of them. In general the expectations seemed a lot lower than what I'm used to, which had a negative effect on the outcome of the course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had teachers who were very similar to what I'm familiar with: a lot of discussions and open questions. But I'm not sure if this is the general way of teaching in Italy.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
English Literature
British Theater
Representation and Image theories
The Western Tradition: Moral and Political Values

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: 'Representation and Image theories' and 'The Western Tradition: Moral and Political Values' were taught by great teachers.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I ran out of free data because I was abroad for a long period, which I didn't expect since I was in the EU. And Milano is in general quite expensive when you go out (often you pay an entrance when going to a club), but of course you can find cheaper place to eat/drink/buy groceries.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee was really cheap and some bars.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You could sign up for sports through the university or join different activities through the volunteering Erasmus group (they also arranged a welcome day).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend joining a sports team through the university since it makes it easier to meet some Italien students in a different setting.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I really recommend visiting Lake Como and hiking to some the refugios in the surrounding mountans. I joined the facebook group International Hiking Milano who arranges different trips almost every weekend. Milano has a lof of museums (PAC, Mudec, Fondazione Prada, Pirelli Hangar), that I would recommend going to - and many private collections and houses like Villa Necchi which are worth a visit.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found most Italians friendly and talkative, but sometimes they could seem a bit cold (mostly in stores/bars). But I think it was easy - especially because the social life in Milano is very vibrant and happens in the city and outdoors. I did find it a bit difficult getting used to the school system and the way information was delievered.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a sport activity and just talk to people in your class. In my experience my Italian classmates were very interested in meeting new people and were often good at suggesting we'd go out for a coffee or an aperitivo after classes. There are cheap bars everywhere, so it's not a big deal to set up.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The social life in the city and all the little bars where you can buy cheap coffee and practice Italian at the counter.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Try to learn some basic Italian beforehand and practice in all the little bars. Most people speak English but are happy to talk Italian with you.
Go hiking on the weekends and take the train to other cities.
Make sure to visit the different areas in Milano (Isola, Porta Venezia, Porta Romana, Loreto etc.) and not just the city centre.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Milano can be very cold and rainy during winter so bring an umbrella and winterjacket, if you're going in the spring semester.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people, being in nature and living in a very different culture and city.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The first few weeks were though because the university didn't plan any real introduction and was quite late on giving information on classes.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
